topic: Decoding the DNA of Linear Transformations: Eigenvectors, Eigenvalues, and Eigenbasis
target_audience: Undergraduate students in STEM or advanced high school students with a background in basic matrix multiplication.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Linear Transformations as Space Warping
lecture_lines: Matrix multiplication warps the entire coordinate space.
Watch our Elastic-Cat stretch under this linear transformation.
Most vectors shift away from their original lines.
animations: Draw a 2D NumberPlane (#1890FF) and a simple 'cat' shape (#FAAD14) made of lines.
Animate the NumberPlane and 'cat' shearing via a linear transformation matrix [[1, 1], [0, 1]].
Highlight several white vectors (#FFFFFF) that have moved off their original span during the transformation.

sections.title: Defining Eigenvectors: The Unchanging Directions
lecture_lines: Some special vectors stay on their original span.
Watch the whisker as the cat stretches diagonally.
It stays horizontal while everything else tilts.
These unchanging directions are called eigenvectors.
They define the transformation's fundamental axes.
animations: Display the sheared 'cat' shape (#FAAD14) on the NumberPlane (#1890FF) from the previous section.
Highlight a specific horizontal whisker vector (#52C41A) that still lies on the x-axis.
Animate the whisker scaling in length (factor of 2) while remaining strictly on its original line.
Draw a dashed line (#52C41A) extending through the whisker to represent its span.
Label the highlighted whisker "Eigenvector" (#52C41A) with a simple pointer.

sections.title: Defining Eigenvalues: The Scale of Change
lecture_lines: Eigenvalues measure how much eigenvectors stretch or shrink.
If the whisker triples in length, lambda is three.
Negative values mean the vector flips direction.
animations: Scale the horizontal eigenvector (#52C41A) from length 1 to length 3.
Display the label 'λ = 3' (#F5222D) prominently next to the stretching vector.
Show the equation 'Av = 3v' (#FFFFFF) with the scalar '3' highlighted in red (#F5222D).

sections.title: The Characteristic Equation: Finding the Secret Directions
lecture_lines: We solve Av equals lambda v for these vectors.
Rearranging gives the determinant of A minus lambda I.
Setting the determinant to zero collapses the space.
This collapse identifies our valid eigenvalues.
Then, finding the null space yields eigenvectors.
animations: Display the equation 'Av = λv' (#FFFFFF) and animate its transition to '(A - λI)v = 0' (#FFFFFF).
Show a 2D NumberPlane (#1890FF) warping dynamically as a λ slider is adjusted.
Animate the NumberPlane squashing into a single line when λ reaches a specific value.
Flash the text 'det(A - λI) = 0' (#F5222D) in bold when the space collapses.
Display the resulting eigenvalue λ (#F5222D) next to the collapsed grid.

sections.title: The Eigenbasis: A Better Point of View
lecture_lines: Eigenvectors can form a natural coordinate system.
In this Eigenbasis, transformations only scale vectors.
This turns complex matrices into simple diagonal ones.
We decompose the matrix using these fundamental directions.
Now, calculating high matrix powers becomes instant scaling.
animations: Construct a new coordinate grid (#52C41A) using two eigenvectors as the basis vectors.
Transform a vector (#FAAD14) on this grid, showing it only scales along the new axes.
Display a diagonal matrix D (#FFFFFF) with eigenvalues on the main diagonal.
Show the matrix decomposition equation 'A = PDP⁻¹' (#FFFFFF) with 'D' highlighted.
Animate 'A^10' by showing the basis vectors scaling by 'λ^10' (#F5222D) instantly.

sections.title: Real-world Application & Summary
lecture_lines: Eigenvectors reveal the core DNA of transformations.
They power Google's search and facial recognition systems.
Understanding them unlocks the heart of linear algebra.
animations: Display a summary flow chart: Matrix → Eigenvectors (#52C41A) → Eigenvalues (#F5222D).
Show a facial outline (#FAAD14) with arrows indicating primary 'directions' of facial features (Eigenfaces).
Fade in the final title: 'The DNA of Linear Transformations' (#FFFFFF) centered on screen.
